requirements.text: Establish platform requirements, organizational owners, billing owners, workload boundaries, environment model, and regional or residency constraints.
Compare viable organization, folder, billing-account, project, and Shared VPC placement models against ownership, isolation, connectivity, and rollout needs.
Select the placement model and state where each capability lives, including the Shared VPC host and service-project relationship.
Name the smallest structural change unit, such as one folder, project set, host project, or region set.
Surface region, residency, connectivity, continuity, and ownership implications that shape the recommendation.

Return the structural objective and requirements, candidate comparison, recommended placement, separate billing and platform ownership, smallest change unit, and material regional or connectivity assumptions.

cases.prompt: Design the GCP organization and Shared VPC placement for a central platform team serving development and production workloads owned by separate business units.
cases.initial_state: A central network team may operate the host project, while workload teams need independent service-project ownership and billing traceability.
cases.expected_output: A structural decision compares placement models, recommends the host and service-project relationship, separates ownership, names the first change unit, and states connectivity and continuity assumptions.

assertions.text: The output states workload boundaries, platform and billing owners, and the environment requirements driving placement.
At least two viable placement models are compared against ownership, isolation, connectivity, and rollout needs.
The recommendation explicitly names the Shared VPC host project and its service-project relationship.
The output names the smallest initial structural change unit and material connectivity or continuity assumptions.

forbidden_actions: Recommend a Shared VPC without naming host and service-project ownership.
Treat billing ownership as identical to platform ownership without examining the boundary.

pass: The response compares realistic topology models and chooses one with explicit host, service-project, billing, and platform ownership.
The first rollout unit and its connectivity assumptions are observable in the recommendation.
fail: The response gives a generic folder diagram with no ownership or Shared VPC relationship.
The response proposes a broad migration without a smallest change unit.

cases.prompt: Choose a GCP project and folder model for workloads that must stay in two residency regions while sharing a platform service layer.
cases.initial_state: Residency and continuity constraints may require separate project families, and the platform service layer must not erase the boundary.
cases.expected_output: A placement comparison makes residency, connectivity, ownership, and continuity implications explicit, selects a model, and starts with a named workload or region set.

assertions.text: The output treats residency as a placement constraint and explains its effect on project or folder segmentation.
The recommendation states continuity and connectivity consequences of the selected regional model.
The output names an initial region or workload set as the smallest structural change unit.

forbidden_actions: Collapse distinct residency boundaries into one project family without justification.
Claim continuity without stating the regional or connectivity assumption.

pass: The selected placement visibly preserves the stated residency boundary and names the resulting ownership model.
The rollout begins with a bounded region or workload slice and states what must be proven before widening.
fail: The output treats residency as a footnote instead of a placement constraint.
The output has no initial structural unit or continuity implication.

cases.prompt: Realign GCP billing ownership for a product portfolio while keeping a centrally operated Shared VPC platform.
cases.initial_state: Business units need chargeback visibility, but network and shared-service operations remain centralized.
cases.expected_output: The output separates financial and platform responsibility, selects a billing/project arrangement, and calls out automation, approval, and connectivity implications.

assertions.text: Billing ownership and platform ownership are named separately where they differ.
The output states where projects, billing accounts, and shared networking capabilities live.
The recommendation addresses chargeback or showback, support paths, and connectivity implications.

forbidden_actions: Assume a billing-account move automatically transfers platform ownership.
Ignore the Shared VPC host and service-project relationship.

pass: The response makes financial responsibility traceable without obscuring network platform responsibility.
The chosen placement and its operational implications are concrete.
fail: The response only discusses billing labels and never selects a placement model.
The response leaves ownership or shared networking ambiguous.

cases.prompt: Define the GCP IAM bindings, workload identity trust, and Org Policy controls for an existing project hierarchy; do not change the hierarchy.
cases.initial_state: The primary deliverable is governance control design, while organization structure is explicitly fixed.
cases.expected_output: The response routes the request to internal-gcp-governance and does not invent a new folder, billing, or Shared VPC placement model.

assertions.text: The response identifies governance as the owner because the requested deliverable is IAM, workload trust, and Org Policy control design.
The response respects the fixed hierarchy and does not return an unsolicited topology recommendation.

forbidden_actions: Redesign the folder or project hierarchy when the prompt says it is fixed.
Treat IAM and Org Policy authoring as a placement decision.

pass: The output routes the control-stack deliverable to internal-gcp-governance.
The output keeps the existing structural boundary intact.
fail: The output proposes folder or project changes instead of governance controls.
The output claims organization structure owns the fixed-hierarchy control task.

queries.query: Design the GCP organization and Shared VPC host and service-project placement for a central platform team.
Choose a folder and project segmentation model for separate development, staging, and production environments.
Realign billing-account ownership while keeping platform and Shared VPC operations centralized.
Place workloads across GCP regions and project families to satisfy residency constraints.
Compare a central Shared VPC host project with product-aligned host projects and recommend a topology.
Choose the smallest folder or project set for the first safe rollout of a new platform structure.
Separate network ownership, workload ownership, and chargeback responsibility in the GCP hierarchy.
Define a GCP topology that preserves regional continuity while isolating regulated workloads.
Define the IAM, workload identity, and Org Policy control stack for an existing GCP hierarchy.
Validate monitoring, backup, restore, and rollout evidence for a GCP topology change.
Compare two GCP placement options and recommend one using cost, risk, and reversibility.
Write Terraform code that creates the GCP folder hierarchy, projects, and Shared VPC.
Design an AWS organization and account structure for separate business units.
Choose an Azure subscription and management-group topology for a regulated platform.
